2026-09-06.q: Paul says the goal of his charge is love that issues from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith (1:5). Which of those three is weakest in me right now?

2026-09-07.q: Paul puts prayer first of all (2:1). What did I actually put first this morning?

2026-09-08.q: Nearly every qualification in 3:2–7 is character, not skill. Which one would my closest friends say I am weakest in?

2026-09-09.q: Train yourself for godliness (4:7). What would training look like this week — not a feeling, an actual practice?

2026-09-10.q: Older men as fathers, younger as brothers, older women as mothers, younger as sisters (5:1–2). Which of those four do I handle worst?

2026-09-11.q: Godliness with contentment is great gain (6:6). What one purchase or change am I convinced would finally make me content?

2026-09-12.q: Verse 15 calls Paul the foremost of sinners — present tense, years after his conversion. Where am I tempted to talk about my sin only in the past tense?

2026-09-13.q: We are told to pray for kings and all who are in high positions (2:2). Who in authority do I criticize more often than I pray for? Pray for them now.

2026-09-14.q: An overseer must be hospitable (3:2). When did I last open my home or my table to someone who could not return the favor?

2026-09-15.q: Bodily training is of some value; godliness is of value in every way (4:8). Compare the hours honestly: which gets more of my week?

2026-09-16.q: Correct without harshness — do not rebuke an older man but encourage him (5:1). When did I last correct someone, and how did it land?

2026-09-17.q: We brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (6:7). What am I holding as though I could keep it?

2026-09-18.q: Paul warns against myths and endless genealogies that promote speculation rather than stewardship (1:4). What do I spend religious energy on that produces nothing?

2026-09-19.q: God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (2:4). Is there anyone I have quietly crossed off that list?

2026-09-20.q: He must manage his own household well (3:4–5). What is the true state of the thing I am responsible for that no one else sees?

2026-09-21.q: Everything created by God is good and is to be received with thanksgiving (4:4). What good gift have I been enjoying without thanking anyone for it?

2026-09-22.q: If anyone does not provide for his relatives he has denied the faith (5:8). Who in my family have I neglected while staying busy with good things?

2026-09-23.q: If we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (6:8). Is that literally true of me? Where is the honest gap?

2026-09-24.q: Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in unbelief (1:13). Where has God been more patient with my ignorance than I have been with someone else's?

2026-09-25.q: There is one mediator between God and men (2:5). Where am I trying to mediate for myself — cleaning up before I will come to him?

2026-09-26.q: Verse 7 requires being well thought of by outsiders. What do the people at work or next door actually think of me?

2026-09-27.q: Let no one despise you for your youth (4:12). Where do I let someone else's low opinion of me shrink what God asked me to do?

2026-09-28.q: The true widow continues in supplications and prayers night and day (5:5). What does my own need drive me to — prayer, or distraction?

2026-09-29.q: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (6:10). Trace one anxiety from this week back to money. What is at the root?

2026-09-30.q: The law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless (1:9). What rule am I keeping to prove something rather than to love someone?

2026-10-01.q: The aim is a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way (2:2). What in my life is loud right now, and is it loud for a good reason?

2026-10-02.q: A leader must be not quarrelsome (3:3). What am I arguing about right now that I could simply let go?

2026-10-03.q: Paul names five areas of example: speech, conduct, love, faith, purity (4:12). Which is weakest in me, and who is affected by it?

2026-10-04.q: She who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives (5:6). What indulgence is quietly deadening me?

2026-10-05.q: Those who crave riches pierce themselves with many pangs (6:10). What wound in my life did I make myself?

2026-10-06.q: Read the doxology in 1:17 slowly — King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God. Which word there is hardest for me to actually believe today?

2026-10-07.q: Christ gave himself as a ransom for all (2:6). What did that ransom cost, and how casually did I treat it this week?

2026-10-08.q: A recent convert may become puffed up with conceit (3:6). Where has a little success made me less teachable?

2026-10-09.q: Timothy is told to devote himself to the public reading of Scripture (4:13). When was Scripture last read out loud in my house?

2026-10-10.q: Children and grandchildren should make some return to their parents (5:4). What do I owe my parents that I have not paid?

2026-10-11.q: Paul says flee these things, and pursue these others (6:11). Name what to flee and what to pursue this week — specifically.

2026-10-12.q: Paul was appointed to service though he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor (1:12–13). What part of my past do I still think disqualifies me?

2026-10-13.q: Men are to pray lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling (2:8). Whose face came to mind just now? What would praying for them cost me?

2026-10-14.q: Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience (3:9). Is there a gap between what I profess and what I do in private?

2026-10-15.q: Do not neglect the gift you have (4:14). What has God given me that I have let go quiet?

2026-10-16.q: Verse 10 lists hidden, unglamorous work: raising children, hospitality, washing feet, caring for the afflicted. Which unglamorous work is mine this week?

2026-10-17.q: The pursuit list is righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness (6:11). Which one is least like me?

2026-10-18.q: Some swerved from love into vain discussion (1:6). What conversation of mine lately was all heat and no light?

2026-10-19.q: Paul distinguishes supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings (2:1). Which of the four has gone missing from my praying?

2026-10-20.q: Paul says let them first be tested (3:10). What is God testing in me right now, and am I treating it as a test or as a nuisance?

2026-10-21.q: Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching (4:16). Which of those two do I neglect — my life, or what I believe?

2026-10-22.q: Paul warns about drifting into idleness, gossip, and busybody habits (5:13). Where does my idle time turn into other people's business?

2026-10-23.q: Fight the good fight of the faith (6:12). What is the actual fight in front of me right now?

2026-10-24.q: Timothy is told to wage the good warfare in line with the prophecies made about him (1:18). What has God already said about me that I should fight from rather than fight for?

2026-10-25.q: Verse 10 says to adorn yourself with good works. What am I adorning myself with — what do I want people to notice about me first?

2026-10-26.q: Not a lover of money appears in both lists (3:3, 3:8). Where does my bank statement disagree with my confession of faith?

2026-10-27.q: Some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits (4:1). What voices am I devoted to that I have never examined?

2026-10-28.q: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honor (5:17). When did I last thank or encourage someone who teaches me?

2026-10-29.q: Jesus made the good confession before Pontius Pilate (6:13). Where has confessing him cost me? Where have I dodged the cost?

2026-10-30.q: Faith and a good conscience are held together; let go of one and the other shipwrecks (1:19). Is my conscience flagging something I have been calling a small thing?

2026-10-31.q: This kind of praying is called good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (2:3). Do I pray as though God enjoys hearing from me?

2026-11-01.q: The church is a pillar and buttress of the truth (3:15). What does that image ask of the way I talk about my church?

2026-11-02.q: Verse 2 describes consciences seared as with a hot iron. What have I done often enough that it no longer bothers me?

2026-11-03.q: The laborer deserves his wages (5:18). Am I generous, prompt, and fair with the people who work for me or alongside me?

2026-11-04.q: False teachers have an unhealthy craving for controversy (6:4). Do I enjoy arguing about faith more than obeying in it?

2026-11-05.q: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander out loud, and says the aim is that they learn (1:20). What do I make of a discipline meant to teach rather than to destroy?

2026-11-06.q: Learn quietly with all submissiveness (2:11). When did I last learn something in a posture of receiving instead of arguing?

2026-11-07.q: Verse 1 calls oversight a noble task. Is there a form of service I have avoided because it looked thankless rather than noble?

2026-11-08.q: Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress (4:15). Is there visible progress in me over the last year? In what?

2026-11-09.q: A charge against an elder requires two or three witnesses (5:19). Have I believed something bad about someone on a single unverified account?

2026-11-10.q: Such quarrels produce envy, dissension, slander, and evil suspicions (6:4). Which of those four has been in my heart this week?

2026-11-11.q: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1:15). If that one sentence were all I believed today, what would change about the next 24 hours?

2026-11-12.q: Paul reaches back to Adam and Eve to ground his instruction (2:13–14). What does it mean that the church's order is rooted in a story and not only a rule?

2026-11-13.q: Sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable (3:2) — pick one and name the specific thing that breaks it in me. It is usually one thing.

2026-11-14.q: Paul rejects a false holiness that forbids marriage and certain foods (4:3). Where do I confuse being restrictive with being holy?

2026-11-15.q: Paul charges Timothy to act without prejudging and to do nothing from partiality (5:21). Whom do I judge harshly, and whom do I let off easy?

2026-11-16.q: Some imagine that godliness is a means of gain (6:5). Have I ever expected God to pay me back for obedience?

2026-11-17.q: Paul calls himself a display of Christ's perfect patience (1:16). Who is watching my life as an example, whether I invited them to or not?

2026-11-18.q: Modesty and self-control are named in the same breath (2:9). Where does my spending or my appearance say something I would not say out loud?

2026-11-19.q: Not double-tongued (3:8). Do I say the same thing about a person to their face that I say behind their back?

2026-11-20.q: We toil and strive because our hope is set on the living God (4:10). What am I working hard at, and what is my hope actually set on?

2026-11-21.q: Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands (5:22). Where have I committed quickly and regretted it?

2026-11-22.q: Read 6:15–16 — King of kings, dwelling in unapproachable light. How does my praying change when God is that big?

2026-11-23.q: Some want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they say (1:7). Where do I speak with more confidence than I have earned?

2026-11-24.q: Paul insists he is telling the truth and not lying (2:7). Who needs me to tell them the truth this week?

2026-11-25.q: Paul is writing about how one ought to behave in the household of God (3:15). If church is a household, am I acting like family or like a guest?

2026-11-26.q: Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths (4:7). What do I consume that leaves me spiritually dull?

2026-11-27.q: Keep yourself pure (5:22) closes a passage about handling other people's messes. How does serving others expose me to temptation?

2026-11-28.q: The rich are told not to be haughty nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (6:17). By world standards I am rich. So what?

2026-11-29.q: Paul thanks Christ for judging him faithful (1:12). Do I believe God sees me as trustworthy, or only as forgiven?

2026-11-30.q: Intercession means standing between someone and God on their behalf. Whose name will I carry into prayer every day this week?

2026-12-01.q: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith (3:13). Where has serving actually grown my faith?

2026-12-02.q: Timothy is a young man told to lead people older than himself. Where is God asking me to step up before I feel ready?

2026-12-03.q: Paul tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (5:23). What does it say about God that this made it into Scripture? Am I caring for my body at all?

2026-12-04.q: God richly provides us with everything to enjoy (6:17). Am I enjoying his gifts, or only anxiously managing them?

2026-12-05.q: The letter opens with Paul asking Timothy to stay in Ephesus (1:3) — a hard place. What has God asked me to stay in that I would rather leave?

2026-12-06.q: This chapter puts the whole world in view — all people, all positions (2:1–4). How small has my prayer list gotten?

2026-12-07.q: Read 3:16 aloud — the six lines about Christ. Which line do I most need to be true this week?

2026-12-08.q: Godliness holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come (4:8). Name one way obedience has already paid off in this life.

2026-12-09.q: The sins of some are conspicuous, and the sins of others appear later (5:24). What in me would surface if my life were slowed down and examined?

2026-12-10.q: Be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (6:18). What is one specific thing I can give away this week?

2026-12-11.q: Verse 11 calls it the gospel of the glory of the blessed God. Where has good news quietly become mostly a set of rules to me?

2026-12-12.q: Verse 15 speaks of continuing in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. Which of those four do I most need continued in, not merely started?

2026-12-13.q: Able to teach (3:2) is the one skill in a list of virtues. Who could I explain the gospel to plainly, in my own words, today?

2026-12-14.q: Be trained in the words of the faith and the good doctrine you have followed (4:6). What is one truth I know well enough to feed someone else with?

2026-12-15.q: Good works are conspicuous, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden (5:25). What good thing can I do this week that no one will see?

2026-12-16.q: Generosity stores up treasure as a good foundation for the future (6:19). What am I building that will outlast me?

2026-12-17.q: Paul lists the lawless in 1:9–10 without flinching or softening. What sin have I stopped naming plainly in my own life?

2026-12-18.q: Paul wants believers praying in every place (2:8). Name a place I never pray — the car, the desk, the kitchen sink — and claim it this week.

2026-12-19.q: Verse 11 asks for people who are not slanderers. What did I repeat this week that I had no business repeating?

2026-12-20.q: By doing this you will save both yourself and your hearers (4:16). Who is listening to me? Name them.

2026-12-21.q: Persistent sin is to be rebuked in the presence of all (5:20). What do I make of a church that takes sin that seriously?

2026-12-22.q: Take hold of that which is truly life (6:19). What counterfeit version of life have I been holding onto?

2026-12-23.q: Paul's whole ministry runs on grace he did not earn (1:14). Whom am I still making earn my grace?

2026-12-24.q: If God is not willing that any should perish, what does my patience with difficult people say about how much I resemble him?

2026-09-06.q: Paul says the goal of his charge is love that issues from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith (1:5). Which of those three is weakest in me right now?

2026-09-07.q: Paul puts prayer first of all (2:1). What did I actually put first this morning?

2026-09-08.q: Nearly every qualification in 3:2–7 is character, not skill. Which one would my closest friends say I am weakest in?

2026-09-09.q: Train yourself for godliness (4:7). What would training look like this week — not a feeling, an actual practice?

2026-09-10.q: Older men as fathers, younger as brothers, older women as mothers, younger as sisters (5:1–2). Which of those four do I handle worst?

2026-09-11.q: Godliness with contentment is great gain (6:6). What one purchase or change am I convinced would finally make me content?

2026-09-12.q: Verse 15 calls Paul the foremost of sinners — present tense, years after his conversion. Where am I tempted to talk about my sin only in the past tense?

2026-09-13.q: We are told to pray for kings and all who are in high positions (2:2). Who in authority do I criticize more often than I pray for? Pray for them now.

2026-09-14.q: An overseer must be hospitable (3:2). When did I last open my home or my table to someone who could not return the favor?

2026-09-15.q: Bodily training is of some value; godliness is of value in every way (4:8). Compare the hours honestly: which gets more of my week?

2026-09-16.q: Correct without harshness — do not rebuke an older man but encourage him (5:1). When did I last correct someone, and how did it land?

2026-09-17.q: We brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (6:7). What am I holding as though I could keep it?

2026-09-18.q: Paul warns against myths and endless genealogies that promote speculation rather than stewardship (1:4). What do I spend religious energy on that produces nothing?

2026-09-19.q: God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (2:4). Is there anyone I have quietly crossed off that list?

2026-09-20.q: He must manage his own household well (3:4–5). What is the true state of the thing I am responsible for that no one else sees?

2026-09-21.q: Everything created by God is good and is to be received with thanksgiving (4:4). What good gift have I been enjoying without thanking anyone for it?

2026-09-22.q: If anyone does not provide for his relatives he has denied the faith (5:8). Who in my family have I neglected while staying busy with good things?

2026-09-23.q: If we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (6:8). Is that literally true of me? Where is the honest gap?

2026-09-24.q: Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in unbelief (1:13). Where has God been more patient with my ignorance than I have been with someone else's?

2026-09-25.q: There is one mediator between God and men (2:5). Where am I trying to mediate for myself — cleaning up before I will come to him?

2026-09-26.q: Verse 7 requires being well thought of by outsiders. What do the people at work or next door actually think of me?

2026-09-27.q: Let no one despise you for your youth (4:12). Where do I let someone else's low opinion of me shrink what God asked me to do?

2026-09-28.q: The true widow continues in supplications and prayers night and day (5:5). What does my own need drive me to — prayer, or distraction?

2026-09-29.q: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (6:10). Trace one anxiety from this week back to money. What is at the root?

2026-09-30.q: The law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless (1:9). What rule am I keeping to prove something rather than to love someone?

2026-10-01.q: The aim is a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way (2:2). What in my life is loud right now, and is it loud for a good reason?

2026-10-02.q: A leader must be not quarrelsome (3:3). What am I arguing about right now that I could simply let go?

2026-10-03.q: Paul names five areas of example: speech, conduct, love, faith, purity (4:12). Which is weakest in me, and who is affected by it?

2026-10-04.q: She who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives (5:6). What indulgence is quietly deadening me?

2026-10-05.q: Those who crave riches pierce themselves with many pangs (6:10). What wound in my life did I make myself?

2026-10-06.q: Read the doxology in 1:17 slowly — King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God. Which word there is hardest for me to actually believe today?

2026-10-07.q: Christ gave himself as a ransom for all (2:6). What did that ransom cost, and how casually did I treat it this week?

2026-10-08.q: A recent convert may become puffed up with conceit (3:6). Where has a little success made me less teachable?

2026-10-09.q: Timothy is told to devote himself to the public reading of Scripture (4:13). When was Scripture last read out loud in my house?

2026-10-10.q: Children and grandchildren should make some return to their parents (5:4). What do I owe my parents that I have not paid?

2026-10-11.q: Paul says flee these things, and pursue these others (6:11). Name what to flee and what to pursue this week — specifically.

2026-10-12.q: Paul was appointed to service though he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor (1:12–13). What part of my past do I still think disqualifies me?

2026-10-13.q: Men are to pray lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling (2:8). Whose face came to mind just now? What would praying for them cost me?

2026-10-14.q: Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience (3:9). Is there a gap between what I profess and what I do in private?

2026-10-15.q: Do not neglect the gift you have (4:14). What has God given me that I have let go quiet?

2026-10-16.q: Verse 10 lists hidden, unglamorous work: raising children, hospitality, washing feet, caring for the afflicted. Which unglamorous work is mine this week?

2026-10-17.q: The pursuit list is righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness (6:11). Which one is least like me?

2026-10-18.q: Some swerved from love into vain discussion (1:6). What conversation of mine lately was all heat and no light?

2026-10-19.q: Paul distinguishes supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings (2:1). Which of the four has gone missing from my praying?

2026-10-20.q: Paul says let them first be tested (3:10). What is God testing in me right now, and am I treating it as a test or as a nuisance?

2026-10-21.q: Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching (4:16). Which of those two do I neglect — my life, or what I believe?

2026-10-22.q: Paul warns about drifting into idleness, gossip, and busybody habits (5:13). Where does my idle time turn into other people's business?

2026-10-23.q: Fight the good fight of the faith (6:12). What is the actual fight in front of me right now?

2026-10-24.q: Timothy is told to wage the good warfare in line with the prophecies made about him (1:18). What has God already said about me that I should fight from rather than fight for?

2026-10-25.q: Verse 10 says to adorn yourself with good works. What am I adorning myself with — what do I want people to notice about me first?

2026-10-26.q: Not a lover of money appears in both lists (3:3, 3:8). Where does my bank statement disagree with my confession of faith?

2026-10-27.q: Some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits (4:1). What voices am I devoted to that I have never examined?

2026-10-28.q: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honor (5:17). When did I last thank or encourage someone who teaches me?

2026-10-29.q: Jesus made the good confession before Pontius Pilate (6:13). Where has confessing him cost me? Where have I dodged the cost?

2026-10-30.q: Faith and a good conscience are held together; let go of one and the other shipwrecks (1:19). Is my conscience flagging something I have been calling a small thing?

2026-10-31.q: This kind of praying is called good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (2:3). Do I pray as though God enjoys hearing from me?

2026-11-01.q: The church is a pillar and buttress of the truth (3:15). What does that image ask of the way I talk about my church?

2026-11-02.q: Verse 2 describes consciences seared as with a hot iron. What have I done often enough that it no longer bothers me?

2026-11-03.q: The laborer deserves his wages (5:18). Am I generous, prompt, and fair with the people who work for me or alongside me?

2026-11-04.q: False teachers have an unhealthy craving for controversy (6:4). Do I enjoy arguing about faith more than obeying in it?

2026-11-05.q: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander out loud, and says the aim is that they learn (1:20). What do I make of a discipline meant to teach rather than to destroy?

2026-11-06.q: Learn quietly with all submissiveness (2:11). When did I last learn something in a posture of receiving instead of arguing?

2026-11-07.q: Verse 1 calls oversight a noble task. Is there a form of service I have avoided because it looked thankless rather than noble?

2026-11-08.q: Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress (4:15). Is there visible progress in me over the last year? In what?

2026-11-09.q: A charge against an elder requires two or three witnesses (5:19). Have I believed something bad about someone on a single unverified account?

2026-11-10.q: Such quarrels produce envy, dissension, slander, and evil suspicions (6:4). Which of those four has been in my heart this week?

2026-11-11.q: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1:15). If that one sentence were all I believed today, what would change about the next 24 hours?

2026-11-12.q: Paul reaches back to Adam and Eve to ground his instruction (2:13–14). What does it mean that the church's order is rooted in a story and not only a rule?

2026-11-13.q: Sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable (3:2) — pick one and name the specific thing that breaks it in me. It is usually one thing.

2026-11-14.q: Paul rejects a false holiness that forbids marriage and certain foods (4:3). Where do I confuse being restrictive with being holy?

2026-11-15.q: Paul charges Timothy to act without prejudging and to do nothing from partiality (5:21). Whom do I judge harshly, and whom do I let off easy?

2026-11-16.q: Some imagine that godliness is a means of gain (6:5). Have I ever expected God to pay me back for obedience?

2026-11-17.q: Paul calls himself a display of Christ's perfect patience (1:16). Who is watching my life as an example, whether I invited them to or not?

2026-11-18.q: Modesty and self-control are named in the same breath (2:9). Where does my spending or my appearance say something I would not say out loud?

2026-11-19.q: Not double-tongued (3:8). Do I say the same thing about a person to their face that I say behind their back?

2026-11-20.q: We toil and strive because our hope is set on the living God (4:10). What am I working hard at, and what is my hope actually set on?

2026-11-21.q: Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands (5:22). Where have I committed quickly and regretted it?

2026-11-22.q: Read 6:15–16 — King of kings, dwelling in unapproachable light. How does my praying change when God is that big?

2026-11-23.q: Some want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they say (1:7). Where do I speak with more confidence than I have earned?

2026-11-24.q: Paul insists he is telling the truth and not lying (2:7). Who needs me to tell them the truth this week?

2026-11-25.q: Paul is writing about how one ought to behave in the household of God (3:15). If church is a household, am I acting like family or like a guest?

2026-11-26.q: Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths (4:7). What do I consume that leaves me spiritually dull?

2026-11-27.q: Keep yourself pure (5:22) closes a passage about handling other people's messes. How does serving others expose me to temptation?

2026-11-28.q: The rich are told not to be haughty nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (6:17). By world standards I am rich. So what?

2026-11-29.q: Paul thanks Christ for judging him faithful (1:12). Do I believe God sees me as trustworthy, or only as forgiven?

2026-11-30.q: Intercession means standing between someone and God on their behalf. Whose name will I carry into prayer every day this week?

2026-12-01.q: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith (3:13). Where has serving actually grown my faith?

2026-12-02.q: Timothy is a young man told to lead people older than himself. Where is God asking me to step up before I feel ready?

2026-12-03.q: Paul tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (5:23). What does it say about God that this made it into Scripture? Am I caring for my body at all?

2026-12-04.q: God richly provides us with everything to enjoy (6:17). Am I enjoying his gifts, or only anxiously managing them?

2026-12-05.q: The letter opens with Paul asking Timothy to stay in Ephesus (1:3) — a hard place. What has God asked me to stay in that I would rather leave?

2026-12-06.q: This chapter puts the whole world in view — all people, all positions (2:1–4). How small has my prayer list gotten?

2026-12-07.q: Read 3:16 aloud — the six lines about Christ. Which line do I most need to be true this week?

2026-12-08.q: Godliness holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come (4:8). Name one way obedience has already paid off in this life.

2026-12-09.q: The sins of some are conspicuous, and the sins of others appear later (5:24). What in me would surface if my life were slowed down and examined?

2026-12-10.q: Be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (6:18). What is one specific thing I can give away this week?

2026-12-11.q: Verse 11 calls it the gospel of the glory of the blessed God. Where has good news quietly become mostly a set of rules to me?

2026-12-12.q: Verse 15 speaks of continuing in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. Which of those four do I most need continued in, not merely started?

2026-12-13.q: Able to teach (3:2) is the one skill in a list of virtues. Who could I explain the gospel to plainly, in my own words, today?

2026-12-14.q: Be trained in the words of the faith and the good doctrine you have followed (4:6). What is one truth I know well enough to feed someone else with?

2026-12-15.q: Good works are conspicuous, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden (5:25). What good thing can I do this week that no one will see?

2026-12-16.q: Generosity stores up treasure as a good foundation for the future (6:19). What am I building that will outlast me?

2026-12-17.q: Paul lists the lawless in 1:9–10 without flinching or softening. What sin have I stopped naming plainly in my own life?

2026-12-18.q: Paul wants believers praying in every place (2:8). Name a place I never pray — the car, the desk, the kitchen sink — and claim it this week.

2026-12-19.q: Verse 11 asks for people who are not slanderers. What did I repeat this week that I had no business repeating?

2026-12-20.q: By doing this you will save both yourself and your hearers (4:16). Who is listening to me? Name them.

2026-12-21.q: Persistent sin is to be rebuked in the presence of all (5:20). What do I make of a church that takes sin that seriously?

2026-12-22.q: Take hold of that which is truly life (6:19). What counterfeit version of life have I been holding onto?

2026-12-23.q: Paul's whole ministry runs on grace he did not earn (1:14). Whom am I still making earn my grace?

2026-12-24.q: If God is not willing that any should perish, what does my patience with difficult people say about how much I resemble him?

2026-09-06.q: Paul says the goal of his charge is love that issues from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith (1:5). Which of those three is weakest in me right now?

2026-09-07.q: Paul puts prayer first of all (2:1). What did I actually put first this morning?

2026-09-08.q: Nearly every qualification in 3:2–7 is character, not skill. Which one would my closest friends say I am weakest in?

2026-09-09.q: Train yourself for godliness (4:7). What would training look like this week — not a feeling, an actual practice?

2026-09-10.q: Older men as fathers, younger as brothers, older women as mothers, younger as sisters (5:1–2). Which of those four do I handle worst?

2026-09-11.q: Godliness with contentment is great gain (6:6). What one purchase or change am I convinced would finally make me content?

2026-09-12.q: Verse 15 calls Paul the foremost of sinners — present tense, years after his conversion. Where am I tempted to talk about my sin only in the past tense?

2026-09-13.q: We are told to pray for kings and all who are in high positions (2:2). Who in authority do I criticize more often than I pray for? Pray for them now.

2026-09-14.q: An overseer must be hospitable (3:2). When did I last open my home or my table to someone who could not return the favor?

2026-09-15.q: Bodily training is of some value; godliness is of value in every way (4:8). Compare the hours honestly: which gets more of my week?

2026-09-16.q: Correct without harshness — do not rebuke an older man but encourage him (5:1). When did I last correct someone, and how did it land?

2026-09-17.q: We brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (6:7). What am I holding as though I could keep it?

2026-09-18.q: Paul warns against myths and endless genealogies that promote speculation rather than stewardship (1:4). What do I spend religious energy on that produces nothing?

2026-09-19.q: God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (2:4). Is there anyone I have quietly crossed off that list?

2026-09-20.q: He must manage his own household well (3:4–5). What is the true state of the thing I am responsible for that no one else sees?

2026-09-21.q: Everything created by God is good and is to be received with thanksgiving (4:4). What good gift have I been enjoying without thanking anyone for it?

2026-09-22.q: If anyone does not provide for his relatives he has denied the faith (5:8). Who in my family have I neglected while staying busy with good things?

2026-09-23.q: If we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (6:8). Is that literally true of me? Where is the honest gap?

2026-09-24.q: Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in unbelief (1:13). Where has God been more patient with my ignorance than I have been with someone else's?

2026-09-25.q: There is one mediator between God and men (2:5). Where am I trying to mediate for myself — cleaning up before I will come to him?

2026-09-26.q: Verse 7 requires being well thought of by outsiders. What do the people at work or next door actually think of me?

2026-09-27.q: Let no one despise you for your youth (4:12). Where do I let someone else's low opinion of me shrink what God asked me to do?

2026-09-28.q: The true widow continues in supplications and prayers night and day (5:5). What does my own need drive me to — prayer, or distraction?

2026-09-29.q: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (6:10). Trace one anxiety from this week back to money. What is at the root?

2026-09-30.q: The law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless (1:9). What rule am I keeping to prove something rather than to love someone?

2026-10-01.q: The aim is a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way (2:2). What in my life is loud right now, and is it loud for a good reason?

2026-10-02.q: A leader must be not quarrelsome (3:3). What am I arguing about right now that I could simply let go?

2026-10-03.q: Paul names five areas of example: speech, conduct, love, faith, purity (4:12). Which is weakest in me, and who is affected by it?

2026-10-04.q: She who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives (5:6). What indulgence is quietly deadening me?

2026-10-05.q: Those who crave riches pierce themselves with many pangs (6:10). What wound in my life did I make myself?

2026-10-06.q: Read the doxology in 1:17 slowly — King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God. Which word there is hardest for me to actually believe today?

2026-10-07.q: Christ gave himself as a ransom for all (2:6). What did that ransom cost, and how casually did I treat it this week?

2026-10-08.q: A recent convert may become puffed up with conceit (3:6). Where has a little success made me less teachable?

2026-10-09.q: Timothy is told to devote himself to the public reading of Scripture (4:13). When was Scripture last read out loud in my house?

2026-10-10.q: Children and grandchildren should make some return to their parents (5:4). What do I owe my parents that I have not paid?

2026-10-11.q: Paul says flee these things, and pursue these others (6:11). Name what to flee and what to pursue this week — specifically.

2026-10-12.q: Paul was appointed to service though he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor (1:12–13). What part of my past do I still think disqualifies me?

2026-10-13.q: Men are to pray lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling (2:8). Whose face came to mind just now? What would praying for them cost me?

2026-10-14.q: Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience (3:9). Is there a gap between what I profess and what I do in private?

2026-10-15.q: Do not neglect the gift you have (4:14). What has God given me that I have let go quiet?

2026-10-16.q: Verse 10 lists hidden, unglamorous work: raising children, hospitality, washing feet, caring for the afflicted. Which unglamorous work is mine this week?

2026-10-17.q: The pursuit list is righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness (6:11). Which one is least like me?

2026-10-18.q: Some swerved from love into vain discussion (1:6). What conversation of mine lately was all heat and no light?

2026-10-19.q: Paul distinguishes supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings (2:1). Which of the four has gone missing from my praying?

2026-10-20.q: Paul says let them first be tested (3:10). What is God testing in me right now, and am I treating it as a test or as a nuisance?

2026-10-21.q: Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching (4:16). Which of those two do I neglect — my life, or what I believe?

2026-10-22.q: Paul warns about drifting into idleness, gossip, and busybody habits (5:13). Where does my idle time turn into other people's business?

2026-10-23.q: Fight the good fight of the faith (6:12). What is the actual fight in front of me right now?

2026-10-24.q: Timothy is told to wage the good warfare in line with the prophecies made about him (1:18). What has God already said about me that I should fight from rather than fight for?

2026-10-25.q: Verse 10 says to adorn yourself with good works. What am I adorning myself with — what do I want people to notice about me first?

2026-10-26.q: Not a lover of money appears in both lists (3:3, 3:8). Where does my bank statement disagree with my confession of faith?

2026-10-27.q: Some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits (4:1). What voices am I devoted to that I have never examined?

2026-10-28.q: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honor (5:17). When did I last thank or encourage someone who teaches me?

2026-10-29.q: Jesus made the good confession before Pontius Pilate (6:13). Where has confessing him cost me? Where have I dodged the cost?

2026-10-30.q: Faith and a good conscience are held together; let go of one and the other shipwrecks (1:19). Is my conscience flagging something I have been calling a small thing?

2026-10-31.q: This kind of praying is called good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (2:3). Do I pray as though God enjoys hearing from me?

2026-11-01.q: The church is a pillar and buttress of the truth (3:15). What does that image ask of the way I talk about my church?

2026-11-02.q: Verse 2 describes consciences seared as with a hot iron. What have I done often enough that it no longer bothers me?

2026-11-03.q: The laborer deserves his wages (5:18). Am I generous, prompt, and fair with the people who work for me or alongside me?

2026-11-04.q: False teachers have an unhealthy craving for controversy (6:4). Do I enjoy arguing about faith more than obeying in it?

2026-11-05.q: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander out loud, and says the aim is that they learn (1:20). What do I make of a discipline meant to teach rather than to destroy?

2026-11-06.q: Learn quietly with all submissiveness (2:11). When did I last learn something in a posture of receiving instead of arguing?

2026-11-07.q: Verse 1 calls oversight a noble task. Is there a form of service I have avoided because it looked thankless rather than noble?

2026-11-08.q: Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress (4:15). Is there visible progress in me over the last year? In what?

2026-11-09.q: A charge against an elder requires two or three witnesses (5:19). Have I believed something bad about someone on a single unverified account?

2026-11-10.q: Such quarrels produce envy, dissension, slander, and evil suspicions (6:4). Which of those four has been in my heart this week?

2026-11-11.q: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1:15). If that one sentence were all I believed today, what would change about the next 24 hours?

2026-11-12.q: Paul reaches back to Adam and Eve to ground his instruction (2:13–14). What does it mean that the church's order is rooted in a story and not only a rule?

2026-11-13.q: Sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable (3:2) — pick one and name the specific thing that breaks it in me. It is usually one thing.

2026-11-14.q: Paul rejects a false holiness that forbids marriage and certain foods (4:3). Where do I confuse being restrictive with being holy?

2026-11-15.q: Paul charges Timothy to act without prejudging and to do nothing from partiality (5:21). Whom do I judge harshly, and whom do I let off easy?

2026-11-16.q: Some imagine that godliness is a means of gain (6:5). Have I ever expected God to pay me back for obedience?

2026-11-17.q: Paul calls himself a display of Christ's perfect patience (1:16). Who is watching my life as an example, whether I invited them to or not?

2026-11-18.q: Modesty and self-control are named in the same breath (2:9). Where does my spending or my appearance say something I would not say out loud?

2026-11-19.q: Not double-tongued (3:8). Do I say the same thing about a person to their face that I say behind their back?

2026-11-20.q: We toil and strive because our hope is set on the living God (4:10). What am I working hard at, and what is my hope actually set on?

2026-11-21.q: Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands (5:22). Where have I committed quickly and regretted it?

2026-11-22.q: Read 6:15–16 — King of kings, dwelling in unapproachable light. How does my praying change when God is that big?

2026-11-23.q: Some want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they say (1:7). Where do I speak with more confidence than I have earned?

2026-11-24.q: Paul insists he is telling the truth and not lying (2:7). Who needs me to tell them the truth this week?

2026-11-25.q: Paul is writing about how one ought to behave in the household of God (3:15). If church is a household, am I acting like family or like a guest?

2026-11-26.q: Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths (4:7). What do I consume that leaves me spiritually dull?

2026-11-27.q: Keep yourself pure (5:22) closes a passage about handling other people's messes. How does serving others expose me to temptation?

2026-11-28.q: The rich are told not to be haughty nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (6:17). By world standards I am rich. So what?

2026-11-29.q: Paul thanks Christ for judging him faithful (1:12). Do I believe God sees me as trustworthy, or only as forgiven?

2026-11-30.q: Intercession means standing between someone and God on their behalf. Whose name will I carry into prayer every day this week?

2026-12-01.q: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith (3:13). Where has serving actually grown my faith?

2026-12-02.q: Timothy is a young man told to lead people older than himself. Where is God asking me to step up before I feel ready?

2026-12-03.q: Paul tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (5:23). What does it say about God that this made it into Scripture? Am I caring for my body at all?

2026-12-04.q: God richly provides us with everything to enjoy (6:17). Am I enjoying his gifts, or only anxiously managing them?

2026-12-05.q: The letter opens with Paul asking Timothy to stay in Ephesus (1:3) — a hard place. What has God asked me to stay in that I would rather leave?

2026-12-06.q: This chapter puts the whole world in view — all people, all positions (2:1–4). How small has my prayer list gotten?

2026-12-07.q: Read 3:16 aloud — the six lines about Christ. Which line do I most need to be true this week?

2026-12-08.q: Godliness holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come (4:8). Name one way obedience has already paid off in this life.

2026-12-09.q: The sins of some are conspicuous, and the sins of others appear later (5:24). What in me would surface if my life were slowed down and examined?

2026-12-10.q: Be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (6:18). What is one specific thing I can give away this week?

2026-12-11.q: Verse 11 calls it the gospel of the glory of the blessed God. Where has good news quietly become mostly a set of rules to me?

2026-12-12.q: Verse 15 speaks of continuing in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. Which of those four do I most need continued in, not merely started?

2026-12-13.q: Able to teach (3:2) is the one skill in a list of virtues. Who could I explain the gospel to plainly, in my own words, today?

2026-12-14.q: Be trained in the words of the faith and the good doctrine you have followed (4:6). What is one truth I know well enough to feed someone else with?

2026-12-15.q: Good works are conspicuous, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden (5:25). What good thing can I do this week that no one will see?

2026-12-16.q: Generosity stores up treasure as a good foundation for the future (6:19). What am I building that will outlast me?

2026-12-17.q: Paul lists the lawless in 1:9–10 without flinching or softening. What sin have I stopped naming plainly in my own life?

2026-12-18.q: Paul wants believers praying in every place (2:8). Name a place I never pray — the car, the desk, the kitchen sink — and claim it this week.

2026-12-19.q: Verse 11 asks for people who are not slanderers. What did I repeat this week that I had no business repeating?

2026-12-20.q: By doing this you will save both yourself and your hearers (4:16). Who is listening to me? Name them.

2026-12-21.q: Persistent sin is to be rebuked in the presence of all (5:20). What do I make of a church that takes sin that seriously?

2026-12-22.q: Take hold of that which is truly life (6:19). What counterfeit version of life have I been holding onto?

2026-12-23.q: Paul's whole ministry runs on grace he did not earn (1:14). Whom am I still making earn my grace?

2026-12-24.q: If God is not willing that any should perish, what does my patience with difficult people say about how much I resemble him?

2026-09-06.q: Paul says the goal of his charge is love that issues from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith (1:5). Which of those three is weakest in me right now?

2026-09-07.q: Paul puts prayer first of all (2:1). What did I actually put first this morning?

2026-09-08.q: Nearly every qualification in 3:2–7 is character, not skill. Which one would my closest friends say I am weakest in?

2026-09-09.q: Train yourself for godliness (4:7). What would training look like this week — not a feeling, an actual practice?

2026-09-10.q: Older men as fathers, younger as brothers, older women as mothers, younger as sisters (5:1–2). Which of those four do I handle worst?

2026-09-11.q: Godliness with contentment is great gain (6:6). What one purchase or change am I convinced would finally make me content?

2026-09-12.q: Verse 15 calls Paul the foremost of sinners — present tense, years after his conversion. Where am I tempted to talk about my sin only in the past tense?

2026-09-13.q: We are told to pray for kings and all who are in high positions (2:2). Who in authority do I criticize more often than I pray for? Pray for them now.

2026-09-14.q: An overseer must be hospitable (3:2). When did I last open my home or my table to someone who could not return the favor?

2026-09-15.q: Bodily training is of some value; godliness is of value in every way (4:8). Compare the hours honestly: which gets more of my week?

2026-09-16.q: Correct without harshness — do not rebuke an older man but encourage him (5:1). When did I last correct someone, and how did it land?

2026-09-17.q: We brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (6:7). What am I holding as though I could keep it?

2026-09-18.q: Paul warns against myths and endless genealogies that promote speculation rather than stewardship (1:4). What do I spend religious energy on that produces nothing?

2026-09-19.q: God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (2:4). Is there anyone I have quietly crossed off that list?

2026-09-20.q: He must manage his own household well (3:4–5). What is the true state of the thing I am responsible for that no one else sees?

2026-09-21.q: Everything created by God is good and is to be received with thanksgiving (4:4). What good gift have I been enjoying without thanking anyone for it?

2026-09-22.q: If anyone does not provide for his relatives he has denied the faith (5:8). Who in my family have I neglected while staying busy with good things?

2026-09-23.q: If we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (6:8). Is that literally true of me? Where is the honest gap?

2026-09-24.q: Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in unbelief (1:13). Where has God been more patient with my ignorance than I have been with someone else's?

2026-09-25.q: There is one mediator between God and men (2:5). Where am I trying to mediate for myself — cleaning up before I will come to him?

2026-09-26.q: Verse 7 requires being well thought of by outsiders. What do the people at work or next door actually think of me?

2026-09-27.q: Let no one despise you for your youth (4:12). Where do I let someone else's low opinion of me shrink what God asked me to do?

2026-09-28.q: The true widow continues in supplications and prayers night and day (5:5). What does my own need drive me to — prayer, or distraction?

2026-09-29.q: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (6:10). Trace one anxiety from this week back to money. What is at the root?

2026-09-30.q: The law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless (1:9). What rule am I keeping to prove something rather than to love someone?

2026-10-01.q: The aim is a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way (2:2). What in my life is loud right now, and is it loud for a good reason?

2026-10-02.q: A leader must be not quarrelsome (3:3). What am I arguing about right now that I could simply let go?

2026-10-03.q: Paul names five areas of example: speech, conduct, love, faith, purity (4:12). Which is weakest in me, and who is affected by it?

2026-10-04.q: She who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives (5:6). What indulgence is quietly deadening me?

2026-10-05.q: Those who crave riches pierce themselves with many pangs (6:10). What wound in my life did I make myself?

2026-10-06.q: Read the doxology in 1:17 slowly — King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God. Which word there is hardest for me to actually believe today?

2026-10-07.q: Christ gave himself as a ransom for all (2:6). What did that ransom cost, and how casually did I treat it this week?

2026-10-08.q: A recent convert may become puffed up with conceit (3:6). Where has a little success made me less teachable?

2026-10-09.q: Timothy is told to devote himself to the public reading of Scripture (4:13). When was Scripture last read out loud in my house?

2026-10-10.q: Children and grandchildren should make some return to their parents (5:4). What do I owe my parents that I have not paid?

2026-10-11.q: Paul says flee these things, and pursue these others (6:11). Name what to flee and what to pursue this week — specifically.

2026-10-12.q: Paul was appointed to service though he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor (1:12–13). What part of my past do I still think disqualifies me?

2026-10-13.q: Men are to pray lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling (2:8). Whose face came to mind just now? What would praying for them cost me?

2026-10-14.q: Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience (3:9). Is there a gap between what I profess and what I do in private?

2026-10-15.q: Do not neglect the gift you have (4:14). What has God given me that I have let go quiet?

2026-10-16.q: Verse 10 lists hidden, unglamorous work: raising children, hospitality, washing feet, caring for the afflicted. Which unglamorous work is mine this week?

2026-10-17.q: The pursuit list is righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness (6:11). Which one is least like me?

2026-10-18.q: Some swerved from love into vain discussion (1:6). What conversation of mine lately was all heat and no light?

2026-10-19.q: Paul distinguishes supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings (2:1). Which of the four has gone missing from my praying?

2026-10-20.q: Paul says let them first be tested (3:10). What is God testing in me right now, and am I treating it as a test or as a nuisance?

2026-10-21.q: Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching (4:16). Which of those two do I neglect — my life, or what I believe?

2026-10-22.q: Paul warns about drifting into idleness, gossip, and busybody habits (5:13). Where does my idle time turn into other people's business?

2026-10-23.q: Fight the good fight of the faith (6:12). What is the actual fight in front of me right now?

2026-10-24.q: Timothy is told to wage the good warfare in line with the prophecies made about him (1:18). What has God already said about me that I should fight from rather than fight for?

2026-10-25.q: Verse 10 says to adorn yourself with good works. What am I adorning myself with — what do I want people to notice about me first?

2026-10-26.q: Not a lover of money appears in both lists (3:3, 3:8). Where does my bank statement disagree with my confession of faith?

2026-10-27.q: Some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits (4:1). What voices am I devoted to that I have never examined?

2026-10-28.q: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honor (5:17). When did I last thank or encourage someone who teaches me?

2026-10-29.q: Jesus made the good confession before Pontius Pilate (6:13). Where has confessing him cost me? Where have I dodged the cost?

2026-10-30.q: Faith and a good conscience are held together; let go of one and the other shipwrecks (1:19). Is my conscience flagging something I have been calling a small thing?

2026-10-31.q: This kind of praying is called good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (2:3). Do I pray as though God enjoys hearing from me?

2026-11-01.q: The church is a pillar and buttress of the truth (3:15). What does that image ask of the way I talk about my church?

2026-11-02.q: Verse 2 describes consciences seared as with a hot iron. What have I done often enough that it no longer bothers me?

2026-11-03.q: The laborer deserves his wages (5:18). Am I generous, prompt, and fair with the people who work for me or alongside me?

2026-11-04.q: False teachers have an unhealthy craving for controversy (6:4). Do I enjoy arguing about faith more than obeying in it?

2026-11-05.q: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander out loud, and says the aim is that they learn (1:20). What do I make of a discipline meant to teach rather than to destroy?

2026-11-06.q: Learn quietly with all submissiveness (2:11). When did I last learn something in a posture of receiving instead of arguing?

2026-11-07.q: Verse 1 calls oversight a noble task. Is there a form of service I have avoided because it looked thankless rather than noble?

2026-11-08.q: Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress (4:15). Is there visible progress in me over the last year? In what?

2026-11-09.q: A charge against an elder requires two or three witnesses (5:19). Have I believed something bad about someone on a single unverified account?

2026-11-10.q: Such quarrels produce envy, dissension, slander, and evil suspicions (6:4). Which of those four has been in my heart this week?

2026-11-11.q: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1:15). If that one sentence were all I believed today, what would change about the next 24 hours?

2026-11-12.q: Paul reaches back to Adam and Eve to ground his instruction (2:13–14). What does it mean that the church's order is rooted in a story and not only a rule?

2026-11-13.q: Sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable (3:2) — pick one and name the specific thing that breaks it in me. It is usually one thing.

2026-11-14.q: Paul rejects a false holiness that forbids marriage and certain foods (4:3). Where do I confuse being restrictive with being holy?

2026-11-15.q: Paul charges Timothy to act without prejudging and to do nothing from partiality (5:21). Whom do I judge harshly, and whom do I let off easy?

2026-11-16.q: Some imagine that godliness is a means of gain (6:5). Have I ever expected God to pay me back for obedience?

2026-11-17.q: Paul calls himself a display of Christ's perfect patience (1:16). Who is watching my life as an example, whether I invited them to or not?

2026-11-18.q: Modesty and self-control are named in the same breath (2:9). Where does my spending or my appearance say something I would not say out loud?

2026-11-19.q: Not double-tongued (3:8). Do I say the same thing about a person to their face that I say behind their back?

2026-11-20.q: We toil and strive because our hope is set on the living God (4:10). What am I working hard at, and what is my hope actually set on?

2026-11-21.q: Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands (5:22). Where have I committed quickly and regretted it?

2026-11-22.q: Read 6:15–16 — King of kings, dwelling in unapproachable light. How does my praying change when God is that big?

2026-11-23.q: Some want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they say (1:7). Where do I speak with more confidence than I have earned?

2026-11-24.q: Paul insists he is telling the truth and not lying (2:7). Who needs me to tell them the truth this week?

2026-11-25.q: Paul is writing about how one ought to behave in the household of God (3:15). If church is a household, am I acting like family or like a guest?

2026-11-26.q: Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths (4:7). What do I consume that leaves me spiritually dull?

2026-11-27.q: Keep yourself pure (5:22) closes a passage about handling other people's messes. How does serving others expose me to temptation?

2026-11-28.q: The rich are told not to be haughty nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (6:17). By world standards I am rich. So what?

2026-11-29.q: Paul thanks Christ for judging him faithful (1:12). Do I believe God sees me as trustworthy, or only as forgiven?

2026-11-30.q: Intercession means standing between someone and God on their behalf. Whose name will I carry into prayer every day this week?

2026-12-01.q: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith (3:13). Where has serving actually grown my faith?

2026-12-02.q: Timothy is a young man told to lead people older than himself. Where is God asking me to step up before I feel ready?

2026-12-03.q: Paul tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (5:23). What does it say about God that this made it into Scripture? Am I caring for my body at all?

2026-12-04.q: God richly provides us with everything to enjoy (6:17). Am I enjoying his gifts, or only anxiously managing them?

2026-12-05.q: The letter opens with Paul asking Timothy to stay in Ephesus (1:3) — a hard place. What has God asked me to stay in that I would rather leave?

2026-12-06.q: This chapter puts the whole world in view — all people, all positions (2:1–4). How small has my prayer list gotten?

2026-12-07.q: Read 3:16 aloud — the six lines about Christ. Which line do I most need to be true this week?

2026-12-08.q: Godliness holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come (4:8). Name one way obedience has already paid off in this life.

2026-12-09.q: The sins of some are conspicuous, and the sins of others appear later (5:24). What in me would surface if my life were slowed down and examined?

2026-12-10.q: Be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (6:18). What is one specific thing I can give away this week?

2026-12-11.q: Verse 11 calls it the gospel of the glory of the blessed God. Where has good news quietly become mostly a set of rules to me?

2026-12-12.q: Verse 15 speaks of continuing in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. Which of those four do I most need continued in, not merely started?

2026-12-13.q: Able to teach (3:2) is the one skill in a list of virtues. Who could I explain the gospel to plainly, in my own words, today?

2026-12-14.q: Be trained in the words of the faith and the good doctrine you have followed (4:6). What is one truth I know well enough to feed someone else with?

2026-12-15.q: Good works are conspicuous, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden (5:25). What good thing can I do this week that no one will see?

2026-12-16.q: Generosity stores up treasure as a good foundation for the future (6:19). What am I building that will outlast me?

2026-12-17.q: Paul lists the lawless in 1:9–10 without flinching or softening. What sin have I stopped naming plainly in my own life?

2026-12-18.q: Paul wants believers praying in every place (2:8). Name a place I never pray — the car, the desk, the kitchen sink — and claim it this week.

2026-12-19.q: Verse 11 asks for people who are not slanderers. What did I repeat this week that I had no business repeating?

2026-12-20.q: By doing this you will save both yourself and your hearers (4:16). Who is listening to me? Name them.

2026-12-21.q: Persistent sin is to be rebuked in the presence of all (5:20). What do I make of a church that takes sin that seriously?

2026-12-22.q: Take hold of that which is truly life (6:19). What counterfeit version of life have I been holding onto?

2026-12-23.q: Paul's whole ministry runs on grace he did not earn (1:14). Whom am I still making earn my grace?

2026-12-24.q: If God is not willing that any should perish, what does my patience with difficult people say about how much I resemble him?

2026-09-06.q: Paul says the goal of his charge is love that issues from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith (1:5). Which of those three is weakest in me right now?

2026-09-07.q: Paul puts prayer first of all (2:1). What did I actually put first this morning?

2026-09-08.q: Nearly every qualification in 3:2–7 is character, not skill. Which one would my closest friends say I am weakest in?

2026-09-09.q: Train yourself for godliness (4:7). What would training look like this week — not a feeling, an actual practice?

2026-09-10.q: Older men as fathers, younger as brothers, older women as mothers, younger as sisters (5:1–2). Which of those four do I handle worst?

2026-09-11.q: Godliness with contentment is great gain (6:6). What one purchase or change am I convinced would finally make me content?

2026-09-12.q: Verse 15 calls Paul the foremost of sinners — present tense, years after his conversion. Where am I tempted to talk about my sin only in the past tense?

2026-09-13.q: We are told to pray for kings and all who are in high positions (2:2). Who in authority do I criticize more often than I pray for? Pray for them now.

2026-09-14.q: An overseer must be hospitable (3:2). When did I last open my home or my table to someone who could not return the favor?

2026-09-15.q: Bodily training is of some value; godliness is of value in every way (4:8). Compare the hours honestly: which gets more of my week?

2026-09-16.q: Correct without harshness — do not rebuke an older man but encourage him (5:1). When did I last correct someone, and how did it land?

2026-09-17.q: We brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out (6:7). What am I holding as though I could keep it?

2026-09-18.q: Paul warns against myths and endless genealogies that promote speculation rather than stewardship (1:4). What do I spend religious energy on that produces nothing?

2026-09-19.q: God desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (2:4). Is there anyone I have quietly crossed off that list?

2026-09-20.q: He must manage his own household well (3:4–5). What is the true state of the thing I am responsible for that no one else sees?

2026-09-21.q: Everything created by God is good and is to be received with thanksgiving (4:4). What good gift have I been enjoying without thanking anyone for it?

2026-09-22.q: If anyone does not provide for his relatives he has denied the faith (5:8). Who in my family have I neglected while staying busy with good things?

2026-09-23.q: If we have food and clothing, with these we will be content (6:8). Is that literally true of me? Where is the honest gap?

2026-09-24.q: Paul received mercy because he acted ignorantly in unbelief (1:13). Where has God been more patient with my ignorance than I have been with someone else's?

2026-09-25.q: There is one mediator between God and men (2:5). Where am I trying to mediate for myself — cleaning up before I will come to him?

2026-09-26.q: Verse 7 requires being well thought of by outsiders. What do the people at work or next door actually think of me?

2026-09-27.q: Let no one despise you for your youth (4:12). Where do I let someone else's low opinion of me shrink what God asked me to do?

2026-09-28.q: The true widow continues in supplications and prayers night and day (5:5). What does my own need drive me to — prayer, or distraction?

2026-09-29.q: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evils (6:10). Trace one anxiety from this week back to money. What is at the root?

2026-09-30.q: The law is not laid down for the just but for the lawless (1:9). What rule am I keeping to prove something rather than to love someone?

2026-10-01.q: The aim is a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way (2:2). What in my life is loud right now, and is it loud for a good reason?

2026-10-02.q: A leader must be not quarrelsome (3:3). What am I arguing about right now that I could simply let go?

2026-10-03.q: Paul names five areas of example: speech, conduct, love, faith, purity (4:12). Which is weakest in me, and who is affected by it?

2026-10-04.q: She who is self-indulgent is dead even while she lives (5:6). What indulgence is quietly deadening me?

2026-10-05.q: Those who crave riches pierce themselves with many pangs (6:10). What wound in my life did I make myself?

2026-10-06.q: Read the doxology in 1:17 slowly — King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God. Which word there is hardest for me to actually believe today?

2026-10-07.q: Christ gave himself as a ransom for all (2:6). What did that ransom cost, and how casually did I treat it this week?

2026-10-08.q: A recent convert may become puffed up with conceit (3:6). Where has a little success made me less teachable?

2026-10-09.q: Timothy is told to devote himself to the public reading of Scripture (4:13). When was Scripture last read out loud in my house?

2026-10-10.q: Children and grandchildren should make some return to their parents (5:4). What do I owe my parents that I have not paid?

2026-10-11.q: Paul says flee these things, and pursue these others (6:11). Name what to flee and what to pursue this week — specifically.

2026-10-12.q: Paul was appointed to service though he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor (1:12–13). What part of my past do I still think disqualifies me?

2026-10-13.q: Men are to pray lifting holy hands without anger or quarreling (2:8). Whose face came to mind just now? What would praying for them cost me?

2026-10-14.q: Deacons must hold the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience (3:9). Is there a gap between what I profess and what I do in private?

2026-10-15.q: Do not neglect the gift you have (4:14). What has God given me that I have let go quiet?

2026-10-16.q: Verse 10 lists hidden, unglamorous work: raising children, hospitality, washing feet, caring for the afflicted. Which unglamorous work is mine this week?

2026-10-17.q: The pursuit list is righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, gentleness (6:11). Which one is least like me?

2026-10-18.q: Some swerved from love into vain discussion (1:6). What conversation of mine lately was all heat and no light?

2026-10-19.q: Paul distinguishes supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings (2:1). Which of the four has gone missing from my praying?

2026-10-20.q: Paul says let them first be tested (3:10). What is God testing in me right now, and am I treating it as a test or as a nuisance?

2026-10-21.q: Keep a close watch on yourself and on the teaching (4:16). Which of those two do I neglect — my life, or what I believe?

2026-10-22.q: Paul warns about drifting into idleness, gossip, and busybody habits (5:13). Where does my idle time turn into other people's business?

2026-10-23.q: Fight the good fight of the faith (6:12). What is the actual fight in front of me right now?

2026-10-24.q: Timothy is told to wage the good warfare in line with the prophecies made about him (1:18). What has God already said about me that I should fight from rather than fight for?

2026-10-25.q: Verse 10 says to adorn yourself with good works. What am I adorning myself with — what do I want people to notice about me first?

2026-10-26.q: Not a lover of money appears in both lists (3:3, 3:8). Where does my bank statement disagree with my confession of faith?

2026-10-27.q: Some will depart from the faith by devoting themselves to deceitful spirits (4:1). What voices am I devoted to that I have never examined?

2026-10-28.q: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honor (5:17). When did I last thank or encourage someone who teaches me?

2026-10-29.q: Jesus made the good confession before Pontius Pilate (6:13). Where has confessing him cost me? Where have I dodged the cost?

2026-10-30.q: Faith and a good conscience are held together; let go of one and the other shipwrecks (1:19). Is my conscience flagging something I have been calling a small thing?

2026-10-31.q: This kind of praying is called good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (2:3). Do I pray as though God enjoys hearing from me?

2026-11-01.q: The church is a pillar and buttress of the truth (3:15). What does that image ask of the way I talk about my church?

2026-11-02.q: Verse 2 describes consciences seared as with a hot iron. What have I done often enough that it no longer bothers me?

2026-11-03.q: The laborer deserves his wages (5:18). Am I generous, prompt, and fair with the people who work for me or alongside me?

2026-11-04.q: False teachers have an unhealthy craving for controversy (6:4). Do I enjoy arguing about faith more than obeying in it?

2026-11-05.q: Paul names Hymenaeus and Alexander out loud, and says the aim is that they learn (1:20). What do I make of a discipline meant to teach rather than to destroy?

2026-11-06.q: Learn quietly with all submissiveness (2:11). When did I last learn something in a posture of receiving instead of arguing?

2026-11-07.q: Verse 1 calls oversight a noble task. Is there a form of service I have avoided because it looked thankless rather than noble?

2026-11-08.q: Practice these things, immerse yourself in them, so that all may see your progress (4:15). Is there visible progress in me over the last year? In what?

2026-11-09.q: A charge against an elder requires two or three witnesses (5:19). Have I believed something bad about someone on a single unverified account?

2026-11-10.q: Such quarrels produce envy, dissension, slander, and evil suspicions (6:4). Which of those four has been in my heart this week?

2026-11-11.q: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners (1:15). If that one sentence were all I believed today, what would change about the next 24 hours?

2026-11-12.q: Paul reaches back to Adam and Eve to ground his instruction (2:13–14). What does it mean that the church's order is rooted in a story and not only a rule?

2026-11-13.q: Sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable (3:2) — pick one and name the specific thing that breaks it in me. It is usually one thing.

2026-11-14.q: Paul rejects a false holiness that forbids marriage and certain foods (4:3). Where do I confuse being restrictive with being holy?

2026-11-15.q: Paul charges Timothy to act without prejudging and to do nothing from partiality (5:21). Whom do I judge harshly, and whom do I let off easy?

2026-11-16.q: Some imagine that godliness is a means of gain (6:5). Have I ever expected God to pay me back for obedience?

2026-11-17.q: Paul calls himself a display of Christ's perfect patience (1:16). Who is watching my life as an example, whether I invited them to or not?

2026-11-18.q: Modesty and self-control are named in the same breath (2:9). Where does my spending or my appearance say something I would not say out loud?

2026-11-19.q: Not double-tongued (3:8). Do I say the same thing about a person to their face that I say behind their back?

2026-11-20.q: We toil and strive because our hope is set on the living God (4:10). What am I working hard at, and what is my hope actually set on?

2026-11-21.q: Do not be hasty in the laying on of hands (5:22). Where have I committed quickly and regretted it?

2026-11-22.q: Read 6:15–16 — King of kings, dwelling in unapproachable light. How does my praying change when God is that big?

2026-11-23.q: Some want to be teachers of the law without understanding what they say (1:7). Where do I speak with more confidence than I have earned?

2026-11-24.q: Paul insists he is telling the truth and not lying (2:7). Who needs me to tell them the truth this week?

2026-11-25.q: Paul is writing about how one ought to behave in the household of God (3:15). If church is a household, am I acting like family or like a guest?

2026-11-26.q: Have nothing to do with irreverent, silly myths (4:7). What do I consume that leaves me spiritually dull?

2026-11-27.q: Keep yourself pure (5:22) closes a passage about handling other people's messes. How does serving others expose me to temptation?

2026-11-28.q: The rich are told not to be haughty nor to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (6:17). By world standards I am rich. So what?

2026-11-29.q: Paul thanks Christ for judging him faithful (1:12). Do I believe God sees me as trustworthy, or only as forgiven?

2026-11-30.q: Intercession means standing between someone and God on their behalf. Whose name will I carry into prayer every day this week?

2026-12-01.q: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great confidence in the faith (3:13). Where has serving actually grown my faith?

2026-12-02.q: Timothy is a young man told to lead people older than himself. Where is God asking me to step up before I feel ready?

2026-12-03.q: Paul tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (5:23). What does it say about God that this made it into Scripture? Am I caring for my body at all?

2026-12-04.q: God richly provides us with everything to enjoy (6:17). Am I enjoying his gifts, or only anxiously managing them?

2026-12-05.q: The letter opens with Paul asking Timothy to stay in Ephesus (1:3) — a hard place. What has God asked me to stay in that I would rather leave?

2026-12-06.q: This chapter puts the whole world in view — all people, all positions (2:1–4). How small has my prayer list gotten?

2026-12-07.q: Read 3:16 aloud — the six lines about Christ. Which line do I most need to be true this week?

2026-12-08.q: Godliness holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come (4:8). Name one way obedience has already paid off in this life.

2026-12-09.q: The sins of some are conspicuous, and the sins of others appear later (5:24). What in me would surface if my life were slowed down and examined?

2026-12-10.q: Be rich in good works, generous and ready to share (6:18). What is one specific thing I can give away this week?

2026-12-11.q: Verse 11 calls it the gospel of the glory of the blessed God. Where has good news quietly become mostly a set of rules to me?
